name: Transesterification and Biodiesel
what: Transesterification is a reaction between an ester and an alcohol, in the presence of a base catalyst, to form a new ester. When plant or animal triglycerides react with methanol or ethanol, the products are fatty acid methyl or ethyl esters, collectively known as biodiesel, along with glycerol.
why: Biodiesel is a renewable alternative to fossil fuel-based petrodiesel. Understanding transesterification connects organic reaction chemistry to real-world sustainability and green chemistry contexts.

items.title: I can classify a transesterification reaction given an equation or description
items.what: Transesterification involves an ester reacting with an alcohol to form a new ester, with the original alcohol being released. The alcohol used in the reaction becomes the new alkyl group of the ester product.
items.why: Transesterification is listed separately from condensation and hydrolysis in the Study Design. Students must be able to distinguish it from esterification (which starts with a carboxylic acid) and from hydrolysis (which uses water, not an alcohol).
items.example: A triglyceride reacting with methanol (CH3OH) in the presence of NaOH gives fatty acid methyl esters and glycerol. Methanol becomes the new alkyl group of each ester product.

items.title: I can write the equation for the transesterification of a plant triglyceride with methanol to produce biodiesel and glycerol
items.what: A triglyceride reacts with three molecules of methanol (or ethanol) in the presence of NaOH catalyst. The three ester bonds in the triglyceride are each replaced by a new methyl ester bond, releasing glycerol. The NaOH acts as a catalyst and is not consumed overall.
items.why: This specific reaction is required by the Study Design. Students need to show the correct reactants (triglyceride + 3 methanol), products (3 fatty acid methyl esters + glycerol) and the NaOH catalyst.
items.example: Triglyceride + 3CH3OH → 3 fatty acid methyl esters (biodiesel) + C3H8O3 (glycerol), with NaOH as catalyst.

items.title: I can explain why biodiesel is considered a more sustainable fuel than petrodiesel
items.what: Biodiesel is produced from plant or animal triglycerides, which are renewable feedstocks that can be regrown. Petrodiesel is derived from crude oil, a finite non-renewable resource. Biodiesel also produces fewer net carbon dioxide emissions because the carbon it releases was recently absorbed from the atmosphere by the plant.
items.why: This connects transesterification chemistry to the green chemistry and sustainability principles in 9C. Exam questions often ask students to compare the environmental credentials of biodiesel and petrodiesel.
items.example: Canola oil (a renewable plant triglyceride) can be transesterified with methanol to give canola biodiesel. Unlike petrodiesel, this fuel does not deplete finite fossil fuel reserves.
